questions.questionText: hour Additional Materials: Multiple Choice Answer Sheet Soft clean eraser Soft pencil (type B or HB is recommended) READ THESE INSTRUCTIONS FIRST Write in soft pencil. Do not use staples, paper clips, glue or correction fluid. Write your name, Centre number and candidate number on the Answer Sheet in the spaces provided unless this has been done for you. DO NOT WRITE IN ANY BARCODES. There are thirty questions on this paper. Answer all questions. For each question there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the separate Answer Sheet. Read the instructions on the Answer Sheet very carefully. Each correct answer will score one mark. A mark will not be deducted for a wrong answer. Any rough working should be done in this booklet.
What confirms that scarcity exists?

options.A: A product has an opportunity cost.
options.B: The demand for a product has risen.
options.C: The government has set a minimum price for a product.
options.D: The supply of a product has fallen.

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the production possibility frontier of a desert island economy where the inhabitants live off just two commodities, coconuts and fish. coconuts O fish What explains the shape of the production possibility frontier?

options.A: Coconuts and fish are perfect complements.
options.B: Coconuts and fish are perfect substitutes.
options.C: The inhabitants consume more fish than coconuts.
options.D: The opportunity cost of fish is constant as more time is devoted to fishing.

questions.questionText: In 2014, there was an outbreak of ebola, a deadly disease, in West Africa. People obtained information from hospitals, radio broadcasts and notices posted by the roadside on how to prevent the disease from spreading. How can these sources of information be classified? hospitals radio broadcasts notices

options.A: private good private good public good
options.B: private good public good public good
options.C: public good private good private good
options.D: public good public good private good

questions.questionText: A rise in the price of a good is accompanied by an increase in the quantity demanded. What could explain this?

options.A: Consumers spend a high proportion of disposable income on the good.
options.B: The price of a complementary good has also increased.
options.C: The price of the good is taken to be an indication of the level of quality.
options.D: The substitute goods are all very much more expensive.

questions.questionText: What causes the demand curve for an inferior good to shift to the right?

options.A: a decrease in consumer incomes
options.B: a decrease in income tax
options.C: a decrease in the price of a substitute good
options.D: a decrease in the price of the good

questions.questionText: In a town, bus fares fall by 50% and this leads to an increase in bus use by 30%. The effect on car use is very low with only a 1% reduction. What is the value of the cross-elasticity of demand between car travel and bus travel?
In the diagram the rectangular hyperbola, DD, represents a firm’s demand curve. D price D O quantity What can be deduced from the diagram?

options.A: An increase in the quantity supplied causes a fall in total revenue.
options.B: The price elasticity of demand decreases as we move down the demand curve.
options.C: The sale of an extra unit gains no extra revenue.
options.D: Total expenditure on the commodity decreases as the price falls.

questions.questionText: What is price elasticity of supply?

options.A: the change in the quantity supplied when a price changes
options.B: the change in the quantity supplied when demand changes
options.C: the comparison of the proportionate change in supply to the proportionate change in demand
options.D: the comparison of the proportionate change in supply to the proportionate change in price

options.A: fall uncertain
options.B: rise increase
options.C: uncertain increase
options.D: uncertain uncertain

questions.questionText: A company opened a garden to the public and charged for entry. The government then provided a grant to improve the garden on the condition that entry became free. What would result from the government’s action?

options.A: The consumer surplus would increase.
options.B: The demand curve would shift to the left.
options.C: The supply curve would be infinitely elastic.
options.D: There would be no equilibrium position as the garden is free.

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the percentages of those on low pay and those on extremely low pay in the UK from 1976 to 2012. A national minimum wage was introduced in 1999. low paid introduction of minimum wage % extremely low paid 1976 1980 1984 1988 1992 1996 2000 2004 2008 2012 year What conclusion is consistent with the diagram?

options.A: The minimum wage helped the low paid more than the extremely low paid.
options.B: The minimum wage reduced the numbers of both low paid and extremely low paid.
options.C: The minimum wage reversed the trend in low pay of the previous 20 years.
options.D: The minimum wage was responsible for the largest reduction of low pay in the period.

questions.questionText: A 10% tax is placed on a good. What type of product would be most likely to face the biggest impact on its equilibrium price as a result?

options.A: one with elastic demand
options.B: one with inelastic demand
options.C: one with infinite elasticity of demand
options.D: one with unitary elasticity of demand

questions.questionText: In 2009 the Australian government made a payment of $900 to those who earned less than $100000 per year. How would the effect of this transfer payment be described?

options.A: neutral
options.B: progressive
options.C: proportional
options.D: regressive

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the market for wheat. S P price P D O X Y Z quantity If the government wishes to fix the price at OP what quantity of wheat must the government buy?

options.A: OZ B XY C XZ D YZ

questions.questionText: As part of a privatisation policy, a government deregulates bus services and sells off its public sector bus services to the private sector. What is least likely to occur following these changes?

options.A: Bus fares are increased.
options.B: Bus service companies invest in new buses.
options.C: Extra bus service companies enter the market.
options.D: Loss-making bus services are retained.

questions.questionText: A government decided to reduce income tax and increase sales tax. The initial equilibrium point is shown by X on the aggregate demand (AD) and aggregate supply (AS) diagram. What would be the equilibrium point after these tax changes? AS AS C AS price X B D level A AD AD AD

What always happens when there is an increase in the Consumer Price Index?

options.A: an increase in consumer expenditure
options.B: an increase in the cost of living
options.C: a reduction in living standards
options.D: a reduction in real disposable income

questions.questionText: What would identify a country with a fundamental balance of payments disequilibrium?

options.A: alternate annual deficits and surpluses in the current account
options.B: a continually growing balancing item
options.C: a large short-term outflow of foreign direct investment
options.D: a persistent rise in foreign currency reserves

questions.questionText: At present, one unit of a country’s currency exchanges for US$1.20. The country aims to set its exchange rate at US$1.00. Which combination of government actions in the foreign exchange market must achieve this aim?

options.A: buying US currency and buying its own currency
options.B: buying US currency and selling its own currency
options.C: selling US currency and buying its own currency
options.D: selling US currency and selling its own currency

options.A: budget deficit
options.B: exchange rate
options.C: money supply

questions.questionText: Possible policies a government might use to reduce a deficit on the current account of the balance of payments include devaluation, government spending cuts, interest rate rises and tariffs on imports. Which two policies would be classified as expenditure-switching?

options.A: devaluation and government spending cuts
options.B: government spending cuts and interest rate rises
options.C: interest rate rises and tariffs on imports
options.D: tariffs on imports and devaluation

options.A: increase interest rates and increase indirect taxes
options.B: increase interest rates and reduce government expenditure
options.C: reduce government spending and increase income tax
